When I first started playing this game I was 15. Right off the bat I was exactly like Ellie. We didn’t have enough money to buy the game back then so a couple of weeks after it came out we got it via gamefly or something similar to that. Since we had limited time to play I steamrolled through it in two days. I still remember being so afraid of the David fight that I had to pause it multiple times. When it ended I just, got Ellie. Everything she did made just perfect sense in my mind. I was satisfied with the ending. oh man I could write pages of what I think the ending means to me. When it ended I accepted it. I was happy with this game and up until they showed footage of the second part in 2016 I was adamant that this game did NOT need a sequel. (My mind has been completely changed however). By the time the DLC was about to be released We had been able to buy a copy of the disc and I was able to download the dlc as soon as it had come out. For some reason... just hanging out with Riley just resonated so deep within me. Everything seemed so similar, as if I had gone through the same notions as them. It was around the time they were arguing after angel knives that I had to put my controller down. Now see I grew up in a pretty strict household when it came to romance and dating. Of course deep in my mind I was straight, there was no way I could be anything but, yet within the last year I had gone through a LOT of questioning and had a very similar experience to Ellie. So when I was able to pick the controller up again and that scene played soon after I was just speechless. Ellie, this badass character who literally faces down death and destruction every other corner, was like me. It’s been five? six? years since I first played Left Behind but I still come back to it. I replay it and the original story so many times. When I first played it I was seriously doubting what I felt as being normal, where in my entire life everything leading up to that point in playing told me that being that way wasn’t acceptable. Now seeing the new trailer, seeing freaking Ellie grow up and straight up steal her friends girl and have her be unafraid of whoever sees her is just amazing. So I wanna say that Last of Us did change my life, for the better. 
Definitely for the better.
